question: 91 + 45 − (33 + 26) + 27 × 2 − 19 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 112.

GIVEN

• 91 + 45 − (33 + 26) + 27 × 2 − 19

SOLUTION

• Bracket: (33 + 26) = 59.

• Multiply: 27 × 2 = 54.

• 91 + 45 − 59 + 54 − 19 = 136 − 59 + 54 − 19 = 112 = 112.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all positives (91+45+54 = 190), add all negatives (59+19 = 78), subtract: 190 − 78 = 112 in one shot.

NOTE

• Always apply BODMAS: brackets → orders → division/multiplication → addition/subtraction (left to right).

question: 79 + 25 − 33 + (14 × 2) + 18 − 26 + 31 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 122.

GIVEN

• 79 + 25 − 33 + (14 × 2) + 18 − 26 + 31

SOLUTION

• Bracket: (14 × 2) = 28.

• 79 + 25 − 33 + 28 + 18 − 26 + 31 = 122 = 122.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 79+25+28+18+31 = 181; Negatives: 33+26 = 59; 181 − 59 = 122.

NOTE

• Group all + terms and all − terms separately to avoid running-total slips under exam pressure.

question:
The line chart given below shows the average number of daily calls per salesperson for six days D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 and D6 of a week.

There were 6 salespersons doing the calling on D2 and there were 9 salespersons doing the calling on D3. What is the total number of calls made on D2 and D3 together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 672.

GIVEN

• Average daily calls per salesperson: D2 = 52, D3 = 40. Salespersons: D2 = 6, D3 = 9.

SOLUTION

• Total = average × number of salespersons.

• D2 calls = 52 × 6 = 312.

• D3 calls = 40 × 9 = 360.

• Total = 312 + 360 = 672 = 672.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Total calls = Σ(average × count). Read only the two needed points (52 and 40) from the chart, ignore the rest.

NOTE

• Average = Total ÷ Number of items, so Total = Average × Number of items — a core data-interpretation formula.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the production of bats by 5 factories. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

What is the total central angle (in degrees) formed by the sectors of D and E?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 198.

GIVEN

• D = 5%, E = 50% of the pie chart.

SOLUTION

• Combined percentage of D and E = 5% + 50% = 55%.

• Central angle = 55% of 360° = (55 ÷ 100) × 360 = 198° = 198.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Each 1% = 3.6°. So 55% × 3.6 = 198° directly.

NOTE

• Whole pie = 360° = 100%; convert any percent to degrees by multiplying by 3.6.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of students in the 5 schools. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

Total number of students in the given 5 schools = 30000.

Total number of students in which of the following combination of schools are 12600?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. B and C.

GIVEN

• Total students = 30000; A=18%, B=22%, C=20%, D=15%, E=25%.

SOLUTION

• Required students = 12600 → percentage = (12600 ÷ 30000) × 100 = 42%.

• B + C = 22% + 20% = 42%. ✓

• So the combination is B and C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert target to percent first: 12600 is 42% of 30000. Then just find the pair of slices summing to 42%.

NOTE

• Checking A+B=40%, C+D=35%, B+E=47% — only B+C hits 42%, confirming the answer.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of laptops sold by the given 5 shops.

Number of laptops sold by which shop are equal to the average number of laptops sold by these given 5 shops?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. E.

GIVEN

• Laptops: A=120, B=150, C=110, D=180, E=140.

SOLUTION

• Total = 120 + 150 + 110 + 180 + 140 = 700.

• Average = 700 ÷ 5 = 140.

• Shop selling 140 laptops = E = E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Take an assumed mean of 140 and check deviations: −20, +10, −30, +40, 0 → sum = 0, so the average is exactly 140, matching E.

NOTE

• Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations; the deviation-from-mean check gives the answer with tiny arithmetic.

question: A chord of a circle is at a distance of 9 cm from the center, and its length is 24 cm. Find the radius of the circle. Also, calculate the distance of another chord of length 18 cm from the center.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 15 cm and 12 cm.

GIVEN

• Chord 1: length 24 cm, distance 9 cm from centre. Chord 2: length 18 cm.

SOLUTION

• Perpendicular from centre bisects a chord. Half of chord 1 = 12 cm.

• Radius r = √(12² + 9²) = √(144 + 81) = √225 = 15 cm.

• For chord 2, half = 9 cm; distance = √(15² − 9²) = √(225 − 81) = √144 = 12 cm.

• Radius = 15 cm, distance = 12 cm = 15 cm and 12 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot Pythagorean triples: (9, 12, 15) gives the radius; (9, 12, 15) again gives distance 12 for the 18 cm chord — no square-root work needed.

NOTE

• For a chord of length 2L at distance d: r² = L² + d². The perpendicular from the centre always bisects the chord.

question: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7:5. How much water must be added to 10 liters of the mixture to make the ratio 9:7?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 10/27 liters.

GIVEN

• Milk : Water = 7 : 5 in 10 litres. New ratio required = 9 : 7.

SOLUTION

• Milk = (7/12) × 10 = 35/6 L; Water = (5/12) × 10 = 25/6 L.

• Let x litres water be added: (35/6) ÷ (25/6 + x) = 9/7.

• 7 × (35/6) = 9 × (25/6 + x) → 245/6 = 225/6 + 9x.

• 9x = 20/6 = 10/3 → x = 10/27 L = 10/27 liters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Milk stays fixed at 35/6. In the new 9:7 mixture, milk is 9 parts → 1 part = 35/54, so total water needed = 7 × 35/54 = 245/54; added = 245/54 − 25/6 = 10/27.

NOTE

• When only water is added, the milk quantity is constant — equate milk in both ratios to solve fastest.

question: Which of the following is the largest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 13/15.

GIVEN

• Fractions: 17/20, 21/26, 13/15, 9/14.

SOLUTION

• Convert to decimals: 17/20 = 0.850; 21/26 ≈ 0.808; 13/15 ≈ 0.867; 9/14 ≈ 0.643.

• Largest value = 0.867 → 13/15 = 13/15.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Each fraction is (denominator − a few)/denominator. 13/15 lacks only 2/15 ≈ 0.133 from 1, the smallest shortfall, so it is largest.

NOTE

• To compare fractions quickly, compare their gaps from 1 (the complement) — the fraction with the smallest complement is the largest.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 0.24.

GIVEN

• (0.008 ÷ 0.04) + (0.0024 ÷ 0.06)

SOLUTION

• 0.008 ÷ 0.04 = 8/40 = 0.2.

• 0.0024 ÷ 0.06 = 24/600 = 0.04.

• Sum = 0.2 + 0.04 = 0.24 = 0.24.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Cancel one decimal place top and bottom: 0.008/0.04 = 0.8/4 = 0.2; 0.0024/0.06 = 0.024/0.6 = 0.04. Add: 0.24.

NOTE

• Dividing decimals: shift the decimal point equally in numerator and denominator until the divisor becomes a whole number.

question: The difference of squares of two consecutive odd numbers is 64. What is the product of the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 255.

GIVEN

• Two consecutive odd numbers n and n+2 with (n+2)² − n² = 64.

SOLUTION

• (n+2)² − n² = 4n + 4 = 64 → 4n = 60 → n = 15.

• Numbers are 15 and 17.

• Product = 15 × 17 = 255 = 255.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b). Here a−b = 2, so a+b = 64/2 = 32 → numbers 15 and 17; product = 255.

NOTE

• For consecutive odds/evens the difference (a−b) = 2, letting you find the sum instantly from a²−b².

The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2520.

GIVEN

• √(7² × 3² × 5² × 6² × 4²)

SOLUTION

• √(a²) = a, so the root of a product of squares is the product of the bases.

• = 7 × 3 × 5 × 6 × 4.

• = 21 × 5 × 24 = 105 × 24 = 2520 = 2520.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Every factor is already squared, so just drop the square root and multiply the bases: 7·3·5·6·4 = 2520.

NOTE

• √(a²b²c²…) = a·b·c… — pull each squared factor straight out of the radical.

The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 23√30 / 120.

GIVEN

• [(√10 + √13)² + (√10 − √13)²] ÷ (8√30)

SOLUTION

• (a+b)² + (a−b)² = 2(a² + b²).

• Here a² + b² = 10 + 13 = 23, so numerator = 2 × 23 = 46.

• Expression = 46 ÷ (8√30) = 23 / (4√30).

• Rationalise: (23√30) / (4 × 30) = 23√30 / 120 = 23√30 / 120.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Use the identity (a+b)²+(a−b)² = 2(a²+b²) to skip full expansion — cross terms cancel instantly.

NOTE

• Rationalise a surd denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by that surd: 1/√30 = √30/30.

question: Which of the following number is NOT divisible by 6?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1473.

GIVEN

• Numbers: 1248, 1356, 1473, 1584.

SOLUTION

• Divisible by 6 ⇒ divisible by both 2 and 3.

• 1473 is odd (ends in 3), so it is NOT divisible by 2 → not divisible by 6 = 1473.

• (1248, 1356, 1584 are all even with digit-sums 15, 15, 18 divisible by 3, so they are divisible by 6.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Scan the last digit first: only 1473 is odd, so it fails the ÷2 test immediately — no need to check ÷3.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 6 = divisibility by 2 (even) AND by 3 (digit sum divisible by 3).

question: 61P0 is divisible by 4. What is the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• The number 61P0 is divisible by 4.

SOLUTION

• A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a multiple of 4.

• Last two digits = P0. Need P0 divisible by 4: 80 = 4 × 20 works, so P = 8.

• (Checking options: 70, 50, 30 are not multiples of 4.) P = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Since the number ends in 0 (a multiple of 10), the tens digit must be even for divisibility by 4 — only P = 8 among the options is even.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 4: check only the last two digits; if they form a multiple of 4, the whole number is.

question: The average of 6 consecutive odd natural numbers is 18. Which is the smallest number out of these 6 numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• 6 consecutive odd natural numbers with average 18.

SOLUTION

• Sum = 18 × 6 = 108.

• Let the numbers be a, a+2, a+4, a+6, a+8, a+10. Sum = 6a + 30 = 108.

• 6a = 78 → a = 13. Smallest number = 13 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For an even count of consecutive odds, the average (18) is the mean of the two middle terms (17 and 19). Count back: 17, 15, 13 → smallest = 13.

NOTE

• In evenly spaced numbers the mean lies exactly at the centre; the smallest = mean − (spacing/2 × (n−1)).

question: The average of 8 consecutive natural numbers is (25/2). These numbers are in ascending order. What is the average of the last three numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 15.

GIVEN

• 8 consecutive natural numbers, average = 25/2 = 12.5, ascending order.

SOLUTION

• For n, n+1, …, n+7 the average = n + 3.5 = 12.5 → n = 9.

• Numbers = 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16.

• Last three = 14, 15, 16; average = (14+15+16)/3 = 45/3 = 15 = 15.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Average of the last three consecutive numbers equals the middle one, i.e. the 7th term = 9 + 6 = 15.

NOTE

• Average of consecutive numbers = the middle value; for 8 terms the mean = n + 3.5, giving the first term instantly.

question:
In the given figure, angle BCD = 145 degrees and angle ABC = 70 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BAC?

[Figure: triangle ABC with side AC extended beyond C to point D; A and B at the base, C at top with D above C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 75.

GIVEN

• Angle BCD = 145°, angle ABC = 70°, with A, C, D collinear (D is AC produced).

SOLUTION

• Angle BCD is the exterior angle of triangle ABC at vertex C.

• Exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles = angle BAC + angle ABC.

• 145 = angle BAC + 70 → angle BAC = 75° = 75.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles, so angle BAC = 145 − 70 = 75° in one step.

NOTE

• Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.

question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 105 degrees, angle EDC = 135 degrees. AB is parallel to DE. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BCD?

[Figure: A–B is a segment; from B the path goes down to C (a valley), up to D (a peak), then to E. AB is parallel to DE.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 60.

GIVEN

• Angle ABC = 105°, angle EDC = 135°, AB ∥ DE.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through C parallel to AB and DE.

• Co-interior angles: part of angle BCD with AB = 180 − 105 = 75°; part with DE = 180 − 135 = 45°.

• But since C is a re-entrant (valley) vertex, angle BCD = angle ABC + angle EDC − 180 = 105 + 135 − 180 = 60° = 60.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• For this Z-with-a-bend shape between two parallels: angle BCD = (angle ABC + angle EDC) − 180 = 240 − 180 = 60°.

NOTE

• When a transversal path bends between two parallel lines, draw a parallel line through the bend and use co-interior angles (sum to 180°).

question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 110 degrees, angle EDC = 140 degrees. AB is parallel to DE. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BCD?

[Figure: A–B is a segment; from B the path goes down to C (a valley), up to D (a peak), then to E. AB is parallel to DE.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 70.

GIVEN

• Angle ABC = 110°, angle EDC = 140°, AB ∥ DE.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through C parallel to AB and DE.

• angle BCD = angle ABC + angle EDC − 180 (bend between two parallel lines).

• = 110 + 140 − 180 = 250 − 180 = 70° = 70.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Directly: angle BCD = (sum of the two given angles) − 180 = 250 − 180 = 70°.

NOTE

• With AB ∥ DE and a valley vertex C, the bend angle = (angle at B + angle at D) − 180°.
